title: Micrometrics Sprint Scrapbook — Isla Cheng
content:
Sprint window: 2025-01-06 → 2025-01-26
Context: small personal OKR experiment to push weekly output while measuring signal/noise on focused work blocks. Working title: Micrometrics — micro-habit tied to measurable output (PRs, docs, evals) rather than hours.

North Star (personal): Increase reliable weekly deliverables that unblock product by 2x while keeping meetings <= 6 hours/week.
Primary personal OKR (draft):
- Objective: Ship dependable, observable changes that reduce inference tail latency and unblock Dedicated rollout.
  - KR1: 3 merged PRs touching serving-runtime batching heuristics (min 1 performance test).
  - KR2: 2 short docs (one runbook, one onboarding note) that cut on-call handoff time by 30% (measured qualitatively in SRE chat + first-run checklist).
  - KR3: Maintain focus ratio >= 75% (measured via daily timer + manual audit).

Week 1 (Jan 6–12) — setup and unblockers
- Monday: sketched microbench harness for prefix caching edge cases. Notes: "start small — instrument, don't refactor yet".
- Tue: paired with Marcus on heuristic landing zone. Result: prototype branch; perf regressions on long sequences. Action: add targeted unit test.
- Wed: quick async design note in PR to capture fallback policy. Slack: #infra-thread ~ pinged on routing-policy.
- Thu: blocked by missing kernel metric; asked Noah for access to experimental perf exporter (ENG-ops).
- Fri: documented debugging checklist (first draft).

Week 2 (Jan 13–19) — experiments and output
- Monday: ran batch of experiments measuring KV cache hit variance. Finding: high variance at seq_len > 1024 in small batches. Hypothesis: current batching policy over-prioritizes throughput, sacrificing tail.
- Tue: opened PR 345 (lightweight sampling + weight cap) — description in linked_artifacts.
- Wed: short retrospective: shipping cadence slowed by context switching. Kept a 90-minute deep block and cleared email backlog.
- Thu: drafted runbook: "diagnose tail latency spikes" — outline + TODOs.
- Fri: synced with SRE to align on alert thresholds (left notes: what to watch, how to roll back quickly).

Metrics snapshot (quick, not fully instrumented):
- PRs opened: 2 (1 prototype, 1 sampling cap)
- PRs merged: 0 (waiting review/bench)
- Focus ratio (self-timer): ~68% (target >=75%)
- Meetings: ~5.5 hrs/week
- On-call handoff doc progress: 30%

Micro-retro (what worked)
- Short, explicit experiments produced measurable signals quickly (kv-cache variance).
- Daily 90-minute deep work block helped push PR text forward.
- Pair session with Marcus accelerated prototype iteration.

Misses / friction
- Context switching for quick Slack asks killed momentum mid-day.
- Perf harness flaky on GPU lab machines — intermittent infra noise.
- Missed one of the doc KRs (not enough time allocated).

Hypotheses to test next sprint
1) Enforcing a per-day "deep block" (2x 90-minute slots) will push merged PR count up by 25% (vs current).
2) Adding a lightweight local perf check (cheap op-count proxy) before CI reduces noisy bench failures and speeds review.
3) Routing policy tweak plus sampling cap will lower 95th percentile by ~8% on synthetic tests.

Next sprint plan (Jan 20–26) — concrete tasks
- Daily: 2x 90-minute deep blocks (calendar-locked).
- Monday: stabilize local perf harness (write script + docker wrapper).
- Tue: address bench flakiness — add retry/logging + doc in runbook.
- Wed: iterate on PR 345 per Marcus comments.
- Thu: finish onboarding note for on-call (checklist + 1 pager).
- Fri: small ship day: aim to merge at least one PR; if not, write postmortem why.

Open questions / notes to self
- How to better quantify "focus ratio" without manual bias? (maybe simple Tally app with categories: deep, shallow, meetings).
- Need to make the runbook readable for non-engineers — include TL;DR and checklist.
- Could we add a lightweight mock service to reproduce long sequence tails locally? Pro: faster iteration. Con: time to build.

Action items (prioritized)
- [ ] Create dockerized perf-check script (due Jan 21).
- [ ] Merge PR 345 or close with learnings (due Jan 24).
- [ ] Complete on-call onboarding 1-pager (due Jan 23).
- [ ] Ask SRE for a standing 15-min sync to triage flaky benches (schedule).

Personal notes:
- Keep language in PRs minimal and clear: problem, experiment, result, rollback. Saves reviewer time.
- Stop overcommitting to meetings — decline or convert to async with clear agenda.
- Celebrate small wins: merged docs, any green bench run is progress.

Links / quick refs:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/345
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-789 (perf exporter access)
- Slack: #serving-runtime thread (pinned message Jan 14)
- Draft runbook: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=eng-tail-runbook-draft

End notes: this is intentionally messy — scratchpad to be cleaned into a more formal OKR doc if any KR looks valuable to scale. If things go well, convert to a public-facing learning note for the engineering blog (short, focused writeup).
